4.97.m: Agastya said: / "Having heard this future account of Vyāsa, O son of Śiva, / I have become full of wonder. Now tell of the sacred fords / that are located here in the Forest of Bliss, O six-faced one! / Tell me of those that have the nature of liṅgas. / Skanda said: / "This very question was asked then by the goddess to the god, O sir; / as it was spoken, I shall tell it; hear it just so, O pot-born [sage]! / The goddess said: / "Whatever sacred fords there are, wherever they are, O Great Lord, / speak of each and every one of them to me here in Kāśī, O Lord! / The God of Gods said: / "Listen, O large-eyed goddess: the sacred ford is declared to be the liṅga; / even in a body of water, the name 'sacred ford' has arisen because of accepting a bodily form. / The forms are Brahmā, Viṣṇu, the Sun, Śiva, Vighneśvara, and others; / the liṅga is celebrated as Śaiva; wherever this is, that indeed is a sacred ford. / In Vārāṇasī, Mahādeva is called the first sacred ford; / north of it is the great well that grants the rank of Sarasvatī. / When seen in the northeast part of the sacred field, it removes the bonds of the bound soul; / after that, Vārāṇasī, endowed with a form, is to be worshipped by men. / When she is worshipped with effort, she always grants pleasant dwelling. / To the east of Mahādeva is Goprekṣa, the supreme liṅga; / from its darśana arises fully the fruit produced by the gift of cattle. / Because cattle were formerly sent by Śambhu himself from Goloka / and arrived at Vārāṇasī, it is therefore remembered as Goprekṣa. / In the southern part from Goprekṣa is that known as Dadhīcīśvara; / from its darśana, men obtain the fruit arising from a Vedic sacrifice. / To the east of it is Atrīśvara, worshipped by Madhu and Kaiṭabha; / having seen that liṅga with effort, one attains the state of Viṣṇu. / In the eastern direction from Goprekṣa, the liṅga is remembered as Vijvara; / by worshipping it, a mortal immediately becomes free of fever. / To the east is Vedeśvara, which grants the fruit of the four Vedas. / North of Vedeśvara is Ādikeśava, the knower of the sacred field; / by the darśana of it, all the three worlds are surely seen. / Seeing Saṅgameśvara to its east, one becomes sinless. / To the east of it is the four-faced Prayāga liṅga, / worshipped by the four-faced creator Brahmā, granting the world of Brahmā. / There, Gaurī who brings peace, when worshipped, bestows peace. / On the eastern bank of the Varaṇā, Kuntīśvara is to be worshipped by men; / by worshipping it, sons are born who brighten their family. / North of Kuntīśvara is the sacred ford called Kāpila pool; / merely by ritual ablution there and by worshipping the bull-bannered [Lord], / 19

Whatever ancestors there are, numbering in the tens of millions, in Raurava and other hells, / 20

North of Goprekṣa, O sage, is the liṅga Anusūyeśvara; / 21
from its darśana, women clearly obtain the reward of devotion to a husband.
In the eastern direction from that liṅga, Siddhivināyaka is to be worshipped; / 22
whatever siddhi one desires, one obtains that by bowing to him.
West of Gaṇeśa is the liṅga of Hiraṇyakaśipu; / 23
there is the Hiraṇya well, which produces prosperity in gold and horses. / 24

West of Mahādeva, O sage, is the Skandeśvara liṅga;
by worshipping that liṅga, humans attain residence in my world. / 26
Indeed, beside that are Śākheśa and Viśākheśa there;
Naigameyeśvara is there, and whichever other attendants (gaṇas) [there are], such as Nandin.

by touching that liṅga, one attains supreme peace.

4.97.m:
Nādeśa is the supreme Brahman; Nādeśa is the highest destination.
Nādeśa is the supreme state, delivering from the sorrowful saṃsāra.
At times the Gaṅgā goes to behold that god;
she is called Matsyodarī; a bath [in her] is obtained through merits.
When the Matsyodarī Gaṅgā reaches Kapileśvara
in the west, O great goddess, then is that conjunction very rare to attain.
To the north of Kapileśvara is the liṅga Uddālakeśvara;
by beholding it, supreme perfection is attained by everyone.
To the north of it is the liṅga Bāṣkulīśa, granting the accomplishment of all aims.
South of Bāṣkulīśa is indeed the liṅga Kaustubheśvara;
by worshipping it, one is never parted from masses of gems.
South of Kaustubheśvara is the liṅga Śaṅkukarṇeśvara.
By worshipping [it], even today an aspirant obtains supreme knowledge.
Aghoreśa is at the cave entrance; to its north is an auspicious well,
known as Aghoroda, which bestows the fruit of a horse sacrifice.

4.97.m:
Gargeśa and Damaneśa are two auspicious liṅgas there,
where the two attained perfection in this very body;
from the worship of those two liṅgas, the desired perfection is attained.
To its south is a great pool remembered as Rudrāvāsa.
Having worshipped Rudreśa there, one obtains the fruit of ten million Rudras.
O Aparṇā, when the fourteenth day is conjoined with Rudra's asterism [Ārdrā],
then is the most sacred time, yielding great fruit at that pool.
A man who bathes in Rudrakuṇḍa and beholds the all-pervading Rudreśvara,
even if he dies anywhere whatsoever, reaches the world of Rudra.
In the south-west direction from Rudra is the liṅga Mahālaya;
in front of it is the Pitṛkūpa, the supreme abode of the ancestors.
A man having performed a śrāddha there should cast the rice-balls into the well;
the performer of the śrāddha, accompanied by twenty-one ancestral generations, partakes of the world of Rudra.
There is an oblong reservoir facing west, named Vaitaraṇī;
a man bathed in it, O goddess, never goes to hell.

4.97.m:
When the celestial denizens travel to Matsyodarī from the heavenly world,
they proceed comfortably by that very path, accompanied by celestial women.
Therefore, O best of sages, that place is known as Svargadvāra.
In the southern part of that pool is a liṅga that bestows the status of Brahmā;
Gāyatrīśvara and Sāvitrīśvara are to be worshipped with effort.
On the charming bank of Matsyodarī is the liṅga Satyavatīśvara;
having worshipped [it] to the east of those two, one's asceticism and fortune increase.
The great liṅga Ugreśvara is located in the eastern direction from Lakṣmīśa;
a mortal becomes a rememberer of past births from worshipping that liṅga.
To its south is Ugrakuṇḍa, which by bathing yields more merit than Kanakhala.
To the west of that pool is the liṅga Karavīreśvara.
From the darśana of that [liṅga], men experience the destruction of diseases.
To its northwest is Marīcīśa, and a pool that destroys a multitude of sins.
West of that is Indrakuṇḍa, and the liṅga Indreśvara, O sage.
To the south of Indreśa is the auspicious stepwell Karkoṭavāpikā.

4.97.m:
Having bathed in the water of that stepwell and seen Karkoṭakeśvara,
sovereignty over the nāgas arises [for him]; there is no doubt of this.
West of that is Dṛmicaṇḍeśa, Hara who removes the murder of a brahmin.
To its south is a great pool granting the fruit of Rudra's world.
To its west is the great liṅga renowned as Agnīśa.
To its east is the pool named Āgneya, granting co-residence in Agni's world.
East of Āgneyeśvara is an auspicious pool to its south.
A man, having bathed in that pool, dwells in heaven with his ancestors.
To its east is Bālacandreśa, who grants passage to the world of the Moon.
All around Bālacandreśa are numerous gaṇa-liṅgas.
Beholding those liṅgas, one attains the station of leadership among the gaṇas.
Near Bālacandra is a well dear to the host of ancestors.
Bathing there, one who offers śrāddha rescues seven [generations of] ancestors here.
East of that well is the holy liṅga named Viśveśvara.
To the east of Viśveśvara is Vṛddhakāleśvara, [who is] Hara.

4.97.s:
kālodo nāma kūposti tadagre sarvarogahṛt ..

4.97.d:

तत्पीत्वा जन्मबंधोत्थाद्भयान्मुच्येत मानवः .. 26 ..

संवर्तेपि न तस्यास्ति नाशः कलशसंभव ..27..

ते रुद्रलोकमासाद्य मोदंते सुखिनः सदा .. 28 ..

4.97.m:
In front of it is a well named Kāloda, which removes all diseases.
Those women and men who have drunk the water there, according to their actions,
for them there is no return here even in hundreds of millions of kalpas.
Having drunk that, a person is freed from the fear born of the bond of birth.
Whatever gift is given at that well to those devoted to Śiva,
there is no loss of it even at the dissolution of the world, O jar-born one.
Those men who carry out repairs of broken and cracked portions there,
reaching Rudra's world, rejoice there, happy forever.
To the south of Kāleśa is Mṛtyvīśa, who takes away untimely death.
And in the northern direction from that well is the liṅga named Dakṣeśvara.
A thousand offenses are destroyed through worshipping it.
East of Dakṣeśa is the great liṅga Mahākāleśa.
A man who, having bathed in the great pool, worships Mahākāla,
by him, indeed, this moving and unmoving universe has been worshipped there.
Having beheld Antakeśvara to its south, there is no fear of Death.

4.97.s:

talliṃgamarcayanmartyo dhanadhānyasamṛddhibhāk .. 34 ..

4.97.d:
हस्तिपालेश्वरं लिंगं तस्य दक्षिणतो मुने..

बंदीश्वरो महाकाल कुंडादुत्तरतः शुभः ..
बंदिकुंडं च विख्यातं वाराणस्यां महाघहृत्.. 36..

4.97.m:
To its south, O sage, is the liṅga Hastipāleśvara.
From worshipping it, one indeed attains the merit born of the gift of an elephant.
There is Airāvatakuṇḍa and the liṅga Airāvateśvara.
A mortal worshipping that liṅga enjoys abundance of wealth and grain.
To its south, for welfare, is the liṅga Mālatīśvara.
North of Hastīśvara is Jayanteśa, who grants victory.
North of the Mahākāla pool is the auspicious Bandīśvara.
And Bandīkuṇḍa is renowned in Vārāṇasī as destroying great sins.
There, by bathing, giving gifts, and offering śrāddha, one attains the imperishable.
There is the liṅga Dhanvantarīśvara and the pool of that very name.
Another name belongs to that liṅga, and another name to the pool:
Tuṅgeśvara is the name of the liṅga, and the pool is named Vaidyeśvara.
Great herbs full of nectar were thrown there, O highly intelligent one.
Therefore, from bathing in that pool and from beholding that liṅga,
all diseases perish, together with terrifying sins.

4.97.s:

4.97.d:
तदुत्तरे हलीशेशः सर्वव्याधिनिपूदनः ..

4.97.m:
North of that is Halīśeśa, the destroyer of all diseases.
And south of the one named Tuṅga is Śiveśvara, the bringer of auspiciousness.
South of Śiveśa is the auspicious liṅga Jamadagnīśvara.
West of it is Bhairaveśa; north of it is an auspicious well.
Merely by touching its water, one attains the fruit of all sacrifices.
In the western part of that well is Sukeśa, who grants perfection in yoga.
To its southwest is Vyāseśa and a well of clear water.
A man, having bathed in the well of Vyāsa and gratified the gods and ancestors,
attains an imperishable world wherever desired.
West of Vyāsatīrtha is the great lake Ghaṇṭākarṇa.
Having bathed in the lake of Ghaṇṭākarṇa, from beholding Vyāseśa,
he, dying wherever he may, dies [as if] in Vārāṇasī.
Near Ghaṇṭākarṇa is the lake of the apsaras Pañcacūḍā.
Bathing in the waters of Pañcacūḍā and beholding that god, Īśvara,
a man goes to heaven and becomes beloved of Pañcacūḍā.

4.97.d:
गौरीकूपस्ततोवाच्यां सर्वजाड्यविनाशनः .. 47 ..
पंचचूडोत्तरे भागे तीर्थं चाशोकसंज्ञितम्..

मुक्तिक्षेत्रप्रमाणं च क्रोशं क्रोशं च सर्वतः..

4.97.m:
To the south of that is Gaurīkūpa, which destroys all sluggishness.
To the north of Pañcacūḍā is the sacred ford named Aśoka.
To its north is the great sacred ford Mandākinī, which removes great sins.
Even in the heavenly world she is holy; how much more among humans, O sage!
To its north is Madhyameśa; ah, the sacred field rests in the middle!
A man who keeps a vigil there on the Aśokāṣṭamī in the spring
never incurs sorrow; he becomes full of perpetual bliss.
The extent of the sacred field of liberation is a krośa in every direction
beginning from this merit-bestowing liṅga, Madhyameśvara.
All the great-grandfathers always say just this:
“May someone born in our family, having bathed in the waters of Mandākinī,
feed, with restraint, brahmins, ascetics, and Pāśupatas!”
A man who has bathed in the Mandākinī and beheld Madhyameśvara
dwells for a long time in Rudra's world together with twenty-one generations of his family.
To the south of Madhyameśa is the auspicious Viśvedeveśvara.
By worshiping it, the thirteen Viśvedevas are worshiped.

4.97.m:
To its east is Vīrabhadreśa, who grants the station of a great hero.
To his south is auspicious Bhadrakālī, bestowing blessings;
the pool named Bhadrakāla there is exceedingly auspicious.
To its east is the liṅga Āpastambeśvara, bestowing supreme knowledge.
To its north is Puṇyakūpa; to the west of that is the pool of Śaunaka.
To the west of the pool is the liṅga Śaunakeśa, granting fine intellect.
A man who bathes in that pool and beholds Śaunakeśvara
obtains that divine knowledge by which he crosses over death.
To its south is Jambukeśa, who averts rebirth as an animal.
To its north is Mataṅgeśa, who awakens the art of music.
To the northwest of Mataṅgeśa are various liṅgas in every direction,
established here by sages, bestowing all perfections.
The liṅga Brahmarāteśvara is to the south of Mataṅgeśa;
from beholding that liṅga, lifespan is never cut short midway.
There is the liṅga Ājyapeśvara and numerous liṅgas of the ancestors;

4.97.m:
Bathing in Daṇḍakhāta following an eclipse brings great merit.
There is the cave of Jaigīṣavya, and there the liṅga bearing that name.
Having fasted there for three nights, stainless knowledge is attained.
To the west of that is the liṅga Devaleśvara, bestowing great merit.
Near it is Śatakāla, [where] the lord of Umā

To its south is Śātātapeśa, granting the fruit of great recitation.
To its west is Hetukeśa, the cause of great fruit.
To its south is Akṣapādeśa, who promotes great knowledge.

To its south is to be seen Bhūtīśa, who produces prosperity for the good. // 76

वैवस्वतेश्वरस्तत्र यमलोकनिवारकः ..
तत्पश्चाददितीशश्च चक्रेशस्तस्य चाग्रतः .. 8 ..
4.97.m:
South of Kalaśeśa is Graheśa, an excellent liṅga;
beholding that liṅga pacifies the affliction of the planets. // 1
West of Citragupteśvara is Yadṛccheśa, yielding great fruit;
south of Graheśvara is the Utathyavāmadeveśa liṅga. // 2
South of it are the two auspicious ones, Kambaḷāśvatareśa;
right there is the spotless liṅga worshiped by Nalakūbara. // 3
To its south is Maṇikarṇīśa, and north of that is Paliteśa;
right there is [the liṅga] that removes old age, and west of that, the destroyer of sins. // 4
To the west of that is Nirjareśa; to the southwest of that is Pitāmaha.
There is also the rivulet of Pitāmaha; a śrāddha offered there bears great fruit.
To the south of that is Varuṇeśa, and Bāṇeśa is to his south. / At the rivulet of Pitāmaha, Kūṣmāṇḍeśa indeed bestows perfection.
To the east of that is Rākṣaseśa; Gaṅgeśa is to his south.
To the north of that are the lords of streams; there are numerous liṅgas there.
Vaivasvateśvara is there, who prevents [descent to] the realm of Yama.
To the west of that is Aditīśa, and Cakreśa is in front of him.

4.97.s:
tadagre kālakeśākhyo dṛṣṭapratyayakṛtparaḥ ..
chāyā saṃdṛśyate tatra niṣpāpastadavekṣaṇāt .. 9 ..
tadagre tārakeśaśca tadagre svarṇabhāradaḥ..
taduttare marutteśaḥ śakreśaśca tadagrataḥ .. 4.2.97.210 ..
taddakṣiṇe ca raṃbheśastatraiva ca śaśīśvaraḥ ..
taduttare lokapeśāstatra liṃgānyanekaśaḥ .. 11 ..
nāgagaṃdharvayakṣāṇāṃ kinnarāpsarasāmapi ..
devarṣigaṇavṛdānāṃ nānāsiddhikarāṇyapi .. 12 ..
śakreśāddakṣiṇe bhāge phālguneśo mahāghahṛt ..
mahāpāśupateśaśca tadyāmyāṃ śubhakṛtparaḥ .. 13 ..
tatpaścime samudreśa īśāneśastaduttare..
tatpūrve lāṃgalīśaśca sarvasiddhisamarpakaḥ .. 14 ..

teṣāṃ mokṣo mayā khyāto na tu te devi mānavāḥ .. 15 ..

4.97.d:
तदग्रे कालकेशाख्यो दृष्टप्रत्ययकृत्परः ..
छाया संदृश्यते तत्र निष्पापस्तदवेक्षणात् .. 9 ..
तदग्रे तारकेशश्च तदग्रे स्वर्णभारदः..
तदुत्तरे मरुत्तेशः शक्रेशश्च तदग्रतः .. 4.2.97.210 ..
तद्दक्षिणे च रंभेशस्तत्रैव च शशीश्वरः ..
तदुत्तरे लोकपेशास्तत्र लिंगान्यनेकशः .. 11 ..
नागगंधर्वयक्षाणां किन्नराप्सरसामपि ..
देवर्षिगणवृदानां नानासिद्धिकराण्यपि .. 12 ..
शक्रेशाद्दक्षिणे भागे फाल्गुनेशो महाघहृत् ..
महापाशुपतेशश्च तद्याम्यां शुभकृत्परः .. 13 ..
तत्पश्चिमे समुद्रेश ईशानेशस्तदुत्तरे..
तत्पूर्वे लांगलीशश्च सर्वसिद्धिसमर्पकः .. 14 ..
रागद्वेषविनिर्मुक्ताः सिद्धिं यांति च पूजकाः ..
तेषां मोक्षो मया ख्यातो न तु ते देवि मानवाः .. 15 ..
मधुपिंगश्वेतकेतू लांगलीशे तपस्विनौ ..
अनेनैव शरीरेण जग्मतुः सिद्धिमुत्तमाम् .. 16 ..
4.97.m:
In front of him is the one called Kālakeśa, supreme, who creates verified conviction.
A shadow is seen there; from beholding it, one becomes free of sin.
In front of him is Tārakeśa, and in front of him is the granter of loads of gold.
To the north of that is Marutteśa, and Śakreśa is in front of him.
To his south is Rambheśa, and right there is Śaśīśvara.
To the north of that are the lords of the world guardians; there are numerous liṅgas there,
of Nāgas, Gandharvas, and Yakṣas, and of Kinnaras and apsarases,
and of hosts of celestial seers, granting various perfections.
In the southern part from Śakreśa is Phālguneśa, who removes great sins.
To the south of that is Mahāpāśupateśa, supreme, who brings auspiciousness.
To the west of that is Samudreśa; Īśāneśa is to its north.
To the east of that is Lāṅgalīśa, bestowing all perfections.
Freed from passion and malice, worshippers attain perfection;
liberation has been declared by me for them, for they are no longer mortals, O goddess.
The two ascetics Madhupiṅga and Śvetaketu, at [the shrine of] Lāṅgalīśa,
attained supreme perfection in this very body.

4.97.s:
tatraiva nakulīśaśca kapileśaśca tatra vai..
rahasyaṃ paramaṃ cobhau mama vrata niṣeviṇau.. 17 ..
tatsannidhau prītikeśastatra prītirmama priye ..
tatropavāsādekasmātphalamabdaśatādhikam .. 18 ..
ekaṃ jāgaraṇaṃ kṛtvā prītikeśa upoṣitaḥ ..
gaṇatvapadavī tasya niścitā mama parvaṇi .. 19 ..
devasya dakṣiṇe bhāge tatra vāpī śubhodakā ..
tadaṃbuprāśanaṃ nṛṇāmapunarbhavahetave .. 4.2.97.220 ..
tajjalātpaścime bhāge daṃḍapāṇiḥ sadāvati ..
tatprācyavācyuttarasyāṃ tāraḥ kālaḥ śilādajaḥ..21..
liṃgatrayaṃ hṛdabjeyacchraddhayāpī tamarpayet ..
yaistatra tajjalaṃ pītaṃ kṛtārthāste narottamāḥ ..22..
avimuktasamīpecyoṃ mokṣeśo mokṣabuddhidaḥ ..
karuṇeśo dayādhāma tadudīcyāṃ samarcayet ..23..

4.97.d:
तत्रैव नकुलीशश्च कपिलेशश्च तत्र वै..
रहस्यं परमं चोभौ मम व्रत निषेविणौ.. 17 ..
तत्सन्निधौ प्रीतिकेशस्तत्र प्रीतिर्मम प्रिये ..
तत्रोपवासादेकस्मात्फलमब्दशताधिकम् .. 18 ..
एकं जागरणं कृत्वा प्रीतिकेश उपोषितः ..
गणत्वपदवी तस्य निश्चिता मम पर्वणि .. 19 ..
देवस्य दक्षिणे भागे तत्र वापी शुभोदका ..
तदंबुप्राशनं नृणामपुनर्भवहेतवे .. 4.2.97.220 ..
तज्जलात्पश्चिमे भागे दंडपाणिः सदावति ..
तत्प्राच्यवाच्युत्तरस्यां तारः कालः शिलादजः..21..
लिंगत्रयं हृदब्जेयच्छ्रद्धयापी तमर्पयेत् ..
यैस्तत्र तज्जलं पीतं कृतार्थास्ते नरोत्तमाः ..22..
अविमुक्तसमीपेच्यों मोक्षेशो मोक्षबुद्धिदः ..
करुणेशो दयाधाम तदुदीच्यां समर्चयेत् ..23..
स्वर्णाक्षेशस्तु तत्प्राच्यां ज्ञानदस्तस्य चोत्तरे ..
सौभाग्यगौरी संपूज्या बहुसौभाग्यसंपदे ..24..
4.97.m:
Right there is Nakulīśa, and Kapileśa is indeed there;
both are a supreme secret, engaged in observing my vow.
In his vicinity is Prītikeśa; there lies my affection, O beloved.
From fasting there for a single [day], the fruit is greater than [that of] a hundred years.
Having kept a single vigil, having fasted at [the shrine of] Prītikeśa,
his attainment of the rank of a gaṇa is assured on my festival day.
In the southern part from the deity, there is a step-well of auspicious water.
Sipping its water serves as the cause for humans not to be reborn.
To the west of that water, Daṇḍapāṇi constantly protects.
To the east, south, and north of that are Tāra, Kāla, and the son of Śilāda.
One should offer that triad of liṅgas into the lotus of the heart with faith.
Those excellent mortals by whom that water has been drunk have achieved their goal.
Near Avimukta, in the north, is Mokṣeśa, who gives the intellect geared for liberation.
To the north of that, one should worship Karuṇeśa, the abode of compassion.
Svarṇākṣeśa is to the east of that, the granter of knowledge; and to its north,
Saubhāgyagaurī should be worshipped for an abundance of great good fortune.

4.97.s:
viśveśāddakṣiṇebhāge nikuṃbheśaḥ prayatnataḥ ..
kṣetrakṣemakaraḥ pūjyastatpaścādvighnanāyakaḥ .. 25 ..
sarvavighnacchidabhyarcyaścaturthyāṃ tu viśeṣataḥ ..
virūpākṣo nikuṃbheśādvahnau pūjyaḥ susiddhidaḥ .. 26 ..
taddakṣiṇe ca śukreśaḥ putrapautrapravardhanaḥ ..
tadudīcyāṃ mahāliṃgaṃ devayānīśvarābhidham.. 27 ..
śukreśādagrataḥ pūjyaḥ kaceśa iti saṃjñitaḥ ..
śukrakūpamupaspṛśya hayamedhaphalaṃ labhet .. 28 ..
bhavānīśau namasyau ca śukreśātpaścime śubhau ..
bhaktapotapradau tau tu nijabhaktasya sarvadā .. 29 ..
alarkeśaḥ samabhyarcyaḥ śukreśātpūrvadiksthitaḥ ..
madālaseśvarastatra tatpūrve sarvavighnahṛt .. 4.2.97.230 ..
gaṇeśvareśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ sarvasiddhikaraṃ param ..

talliṃgasparśanādāśu brahmahāpi viśudhyati ..
4.97.d:
विश्वेशाद्दक्षिणेभागे निकुंभेशः प्रयत्नतः ..
क्षेत्रक्षेमकरः पूज्यस्तत्पश्चाद्विघ्ननायकः .. 25 ..
सर्वविघ्नच्छिदभ्यर्च्यश्चतुर्थ्यां तु विशेषतः ..
विरूपाक्षो निकुंभेशाद्वह्नौ पूज्यः सुसिद्धिदः .. 26 ..
तद्दक्षिणे च शुक्रेशः पुत्रपौत्रप्रवर्धनः ..
तदुदीच्यां महालिंगं देवयानीश्वराभिधम्.. 27 ..
शुक्रेशादग्रतः पूज्यः कचेश इति संज्ञितः ..
शुक्रकूपमुपस्पृश्य हयमेधफलं लभेत् .. 28 ..
भवानीशौ नमस्यौ च शुक्रेशात्पश्चिमे शुभौ ..
भक्तपोतप्रदौ तौ तु निजभक्तस्य सर्वदा .. 29 ..
अलर्केशः समभ्यर्च्यः शुक्रेशात्पूर्वदिक्स्थितः ..
मदालसेश्वरस्तत्र तत्पूर्वे सर्वविघ्नहृत् .. 4.2.97.230 ..
गणेश्वरेश्वरं लिंगं सर्वसिद्धिकरं परम् ..
हत्वा लंकेश्वरं विप्र रघुणाथ प्रतिष्ठितम् ..31..
तल्लिंगस्पर्शनादाशु ब्रह्महापि विशुध्यति ..
4.97.m:
To the south of Viśveśa, Nikumbheśa should be worshipped with effort
as the granter of welfare to the sacred field; to his west is the Leader of Obstacles.
The destroyer of all obstacles should be worshipped, especially on the fourth [tithi].
In the fire direction from Nikumbheśa, Virūpākṣa should be worshipped, bestowing genuine perfection.
To the south of that is Śukreśa, who increases sons and grandsons.
To the north of that is the great liṅga named Devayānīśvara.
In front of Śukreśa, the one called Kaceśa should be worshipped.
Having touched the water of the Well of Śukra, one obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice.
Bhavānī and Īśa, both auspicious, should be bowed to west of Śukreśa;
they always provide a raft of devotion for their own devotee.
Alarkeśa, situated to the east of Śukreśa, is to be thoroughly worshipped.
Madālaseśvara is there, to the east of that, removing all obstacles.
The liṅga Gaṇeśvareśvara bestows all supreme perfections;
it was installed by Raghu’s lord, O brahmin, after killing the lord of Laṅkā.
From touching that liṅga, even a killer of a brahmin is swiftly purified.

4.97.s:
mahāpuṇyapradaṃ cānyattatrārcyaṃ tripurāṃtakam .. 32 ..
dattātreyeśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ tasya paścimataḥ śubham ..
tadyāmyāṃ harikeśeśo gokarṇeśastataḥ param .. 33 ..
sarastadagre pāpaghnaṃ tatpaścācca dhruveśvaraḥ ..
tadagre dhuvakuṃḍaṃ ca pitṛprītikaraṃ param .. 34 ..
taduttarapiśāceśaḥ paiśācya padahārakaḥ ..
pitrīśastadyamadiśi pitṛkuṃḍaṃ tadagrataḥ .. 35 ..
tatra śrāddhakṛtāṃ puṃsāṃ tuṣyeyuḥ prapitāmahāḥ..
agre dhruveśāttāreśo vaidyanāthaḥ sa eva hi .. 36 ..
tannairṛtyāṃ manoliṃgaṃ vaṃśavṛddhikaraṃ param ..
priyavrateśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ vaidyanāthapurogatam.. 37 ..
tadyāmyāṃ mucukuṃdeśastatpārśve gautameśvaraḥ ..
tatpaścimena bhadreśtadyāmyāmṛṣyaśṛṃgiṇaḥ .. 38 ..

4.97.d:
महापुण्यप्रदं चान्यत्तत्रार्च्यं त्रिपुरांतकम् .. 32 ..
दत्तात्रेयेश्वरं लिंगं तस्य पश्चिमतः शुभम् ..
तद्याम्यां हरिकेशेशो गोकर्णेशस्ततः परम् .. 33 ..
सरस्तदग्रे पापघ्नं तत्पश्चाच्च ध्रुवेश्वरः ..
तदग्रे धुवकुंडं च पितृप्रीतिकरं परम् .. 34 ..
तदुत्तरपिशाचेशः पैशाच्य पदहारकः ..
पित्रीशस्तद्यमदिशि पितृकुंडं तदग्रतः .. 35 ..
तत्र श्राद्धकृतां पुंसां तुष्येयुः प्रपितामहाः..
अग्रे ध्रुवेशात्तारेशो वैद्यनाथः स एव हि .. 36 ..
तन्नैरृत्यां मनोलिंगं वंशवृद्धिकरं परम् ..
प्रियव्रतेश्वरं लिंगं वैद्यनाथपुरोगतम्.. 37 ..
तद्याम्यां मुचुकुंदेशस्तत्पार्श्वे गौतमेश्वरः ..
तत्पश्चिमेन भद्रेश्तद्याम्यामृष्यशृंगिणः .. 38 ..
ब्रह्मेशस्तत्पुरस्ताच्च पर्जन्येशस्तदीशगः ..

4.97.m:
Another liṅga, Tripurāntaka, granting great merit, should be worshipped there.
The auspicious liṅga Dattātreyeśvara is to the west of it.
To the south of that is Harikeśeśa; Gokarṇeśa is after that.
In front of it is a lake that destroys sin; and to the west of that is Dhruveśvara.
In front of that is the pool Dhruvakuṇḍa, which greatly pleases the ancestors.
To the north of that is Piśāceśa, who takes away the condition of being a piśāca.
In its southern direction is Pitrīśa, and before it is the Pitṛkuṇḍa.
The paternal great-grandfathers are pleased with men who perform śrāddha there.
Ahead of Dhruveśa is Tāreśa, who is indeed Vaidyanātha.
To its southwest is the Manoliṅga, supreme in causing the increase of one's lineage.
The liṅga Priyavrateśvara stands in front of Vaidyanātha.
To its south is Mucukundeśa, and beside it is Gautameśvara.
To its west is Bhadreśa; to its south, [the liṅga] of Ṛṣyaśṛṅga.
Before it is Brahmeśa, and to its northeast is Parjanyeśa.
To its east is Nahuṣeśa, and Viśālākṣī is in front of it.

4.97.s:

tatra viśvāvasorliṃgaṃ muṃḍeśastatra pūrvataḥ ..
taddakṣiṇe vidhīśaśca tadyāmyāṃ vājimedhakaḥ ..43 ..
daśāśvamedhike snātvā dṛṣṭvā talliṃgamuttamam ..
daśānāmaśvamedhānāṃ phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ .. 44 ..

4.97.d:
विशालाक्षीश्वरं लिंगं तत्रैव क्षेत्रवस्तिदम् ..
जरासंधेश्वरं लिंगं तद्याम्यां ज्वरनाशनम् .. 4.2.97.240 ..
तत्पुरस्ताद्धिरण्याक्षलिंगं पूज्यं हिरण्यदम् ..

तदग्रे च दिलीपेशो ब्रह्मेशात्पश्चिमे मुने ..
तत्र लिंगं सकुंडं च स्नातुरिष्टफलप्रदम् .. 42 ..
तत्र विश्वावसोर्लिंगं मुंडेशस्तत्र पूर्वतः ..
तद्दक्षिणे विधीशश्च तद्याम्यां वाजिमेधकः ..43 ..
दशाश्वमेधिके स्नात्वा दृष्ट्वा तल्लिंगमुत्तमम् ..
दशानामश्वमेधानां फलं प्राप्नोति मानवः .. 44 ..
तदुत्तरे मातृतीर्थं स्नातुर्जन्मभयापहृत् ..
तत्र स्नानं तु यकुर्यान्नारी वा पुरुषोपि वा .. 45 ..

4.97.m:
The liṅga Viśālākṣīśvara right there grants residence in the sacred field.
To its south is the liṅga Jarāsandheśvara, which destroys fevers.
In front of it is the Hiraṇyākṣaliṅga, worthy of worship, granting gold.
To its west is Gayādhīśa; to its west is Bhagīratha.
Ahead of it is Dilīpeśa, to the west of Brahmeśa, O sage.
There is a liṅga along with a pool, bestowing desired fruit upon one who bathes.
There is the liṅga of Viśvāvasu; there, to the east, is Muṇḍeśa.
To its south is Vidhīśa, and to its south is Vājimedhaka.
Having bathed at Daśāśvamedhika and seen that excellent liṅga,
a person obtains the fruit of ten horse-sacrifices.
To its north is the Mātṛtīrtha, which removes the fear of rebirth for the bather.
Whoever performs ritual ablution there, whether a woman or a man,
obtains the desired fruit through the grace of the Mothers.
To the south of your pool is the supreme Puṣpadanteśvara.
In its southeast direction are numerous liṅgas of divine seers and gaṇas.

4.97.s:
puṣpadaṃtāddakṣiṇataḥ siddhīśaḥ parasiddhidaḥ .. 47 ..

तद्दक्षिणे च क्षेमेशश्चित्रांगेशस्ततो यमे .. 49 ..

चंद्रसूर्यान्वयैर्भूपैः केदाराद्दक्षिणापथे .. 4.2.97.250 ..
प्रतिष्ठितानि लिंगानि शतशोथ सहस्रशः ..
लोलार्काद्दक्षिणाशायां सर्वाशापूरकोर्चितः .. 51 ..
करंधमेश्वरं लिंगं तत्प्रतीच्यां महाफलम् ..

4.97.m:
To the south of Puṣpadanta is Siddhīśa, bestower of supreme accomplishment.
Through fivefold worship, he grants supreme accomplishment in a dream.
Men attain kingship through the worship of Hariścandreśa.
To its west is Nairṛteśa, and then to the south is Aṅgiraseśa.
To its south is Kṣemeśa, and then to the south is Citrāṅgeśa.
To its south is Kedāra, granting attendance upon Rudra.
In the southern region from Kedāra, by kings of the lunar and solar dynasties,
hundreds and thousands of liṅgas were consecrated.
In the southern direction from Lolārka is worshipped the fulfiller of all hopes.
To its west is the liṅga Karandhameśvara, yielding great fruit.
To its west is Mahādurgā, destroyer of great distress.
To its south is Śuṣkeśvara, worshipped by the dry river.
To its west is Janakeśa; to its north is Śaṅkukarṇa.
To its east is the liṅga Mahāsiddhīśvara, granting all accomplishments.
A person having bathed in the Siddhakuṇḍa and seen the great Siddheśvara,

4.97.s:
sarvāsāmeva siddhīnāṃ pāraṃ gacchati mānavaḥ ..

4.97.m:
that human being reaches the limit of all accomplishments whatsoever.
To the northwest of Śaṅkukarṇeśa is the liṅga named Vāḍavya.
In front of it is Vibhāṇḍeśa; to its north is Kaholeśa.
There is the liṅga Dvāreśvara, and the auspicious goddess Dvāreśvarī.
From their worship comes accomplishment, granting residence in the Forest of Bliss.
And there are the protecting gaṇas with various forms and weapons, O sage.
Right there is Haridīśa, and next the liṅga Kātyāyana.
Beside it is Jāṅgaleśa, and behind it is Mukuṭeśvara.
Right there is a pure pool that bestows the fruit of all pilgrimages.
Having bathed in the Mukuṭakuṇḍa and seen Mukuṭeśvara indeed,
whatever fruit comes from the pilgrimage to all liṅgas is obtained.
That supreme earth is the giver of accomplishment in austerity and yoga.
There are, O sage, one hundred thousand liṅgas for accomplishment.
The single northern direction, O goddess, in Vārāṇasī is dear to me.
Even there, my delight is exceedingly in the Pañcāyatana, O beloved.

4.97.m:
Even at the time of creation and maintenance, I am always present there.
He who knows thus is not smeared by sins.
True, true, again true, thrice true, not otherwise, O beloved!
One should go there swiftly if one desires my abode.
Only a brief mention of the liṅgas has been told by me, O sage.
Some liṅgas were established twice or thrice with devotion.
Those that are not mentioned again are to be worshipped with faith everywhere.
All these liṅgas, these sacred pools, these wells,
and these stepwells should be revered by the wise.
From seeing them and bathing [in them], the fruit here increases more and more.
And of the liṅgas, wells, and lakes belonging here,
as well as the stepwells and images, who could be capable of counting them?
Even the blades of grass located in Ānandakānana are far superior [to all else];
for even the gods do not have their rebirth elsewhere.
Kāśī consists of all liṅgas; it is the sole birthplace of all sacred fords.

4.97.d:
स्वर्गापवर्गयोर्दात्री दृष्टा देहांतसेविता ..
मम प्रियतमा देवि त्वमेव तपसो बलात् .. 4.2.97.270 ..

ये काश्यानाम गृह्णंति येनुमोदंत एव हि .. 71 ..

4.97.m:
It grants heaven and liberation when seen, and is resorted to at the end of bodily life.
O goddess, you alone are dearest to me by virtue of your austerity;
yet this Kāśī is naturally my resting place of delight.
Those who utter the name of Kāśī, and indeed those who rejoice in it,
are equal to Śākha and Viśākha to me, like Skanda, Nandin, and Gajāsya.
They alone are my devotees, O goddess; they alone are my attendants.
Those who dwell in Ānandavana are the only true seekers of liberation here;
by them great austerity has been practiced, by them a great vow has been performed,
and by them great gifts have been given—those who dwell in Ānandavana.
They have indeed bathed in all sacred fords, they are consecrated for all sacrifices,
and they have carried out all duties—those who dwell in Ānandavana.
All gods, asuras, uragas, and men are a burden to the earth
who, even in the final stage of life, are not dwellers in Ānandavana here.
Even an outcaste in Kāśī is superior to a master of the Vedic scriptures elsewhere;
the former has crossed the ocean of worldly existence, while the latter is lower even than an outcaste.
He alone is truly omniscient, he alone has additional eyes [of wisdom],

4.97.m:
who, shedding his earthly body in Kāśī, assumes one made of nectar.
Having heard this auspicious chapter which contains the secret of all sacred fords,
a person unfailingly attains the merit born of the darśana of Kāśī.
Whoever recites this chapter every morning day after day,
has seen all these sacred fords; it is not otherwise.
The wise person who constantly recites this chapter consisting of all the liṅgas,
him Yama does not torment, nor his messengers, nor does any sin afflict him.
The fruit of a Brahmayajña accrues to that righteous soul
who, pure and with mind focused upon it, recites this chapter.
He has bathed in all the sacred pools, and he has drunk the water of all stepwells;
he is a worshipper of all liṅgas here, who recites this chapter.
What is the use of many other hymns that bestow exceedingly little fruit?
This chapter, which bears great fruit, must be recited by those who love me.
Whatever fruit is attained here when great gifts are given,

that is certainly gained from the recitation of this.
This itself is the most severe austerity; this itself is the great recitation,
that this chapter named Kāśīliṅgāvalī should be recited, O sage.
To one who hates me, to an atheist, and to one devoted to reviling the Vedas,
this recitation must not be given, must not be given, must not be given.
From the recitation of this chapter, the sin arising from slaying a brahmin,
from approaching forbidden women, and likewise from eating forbidden food,
the sin born of infidelity with the guru’s wife, arising from the theft of gold,
born of slaying one’s mother or father, arising from the killing of a cow or a fetus,
great sins and minor sins, committed knowingly or unknowingly in great numbers,
and the sins born of mind, speech, and body—
all of them vanish completely, beyond doubt, by my command.
Sons, grandsons, wealth, grain, a wife, land,
whatever is desired in the heart, heaven, and also the joys of liberation—
having recited this chapter, the wise person will surely attain all this; there is no doubt.

4.97.m:
While the Lord was thus narrating the story before the goddess,
Nandin arrived, bowed down, and reported as follows:
"The construction of the great temple has reached completion;
this chariot is made ready, and the gods headed by Brahmā have gathered."
Mounted on Garuḍa, the lotus-eyed [Viṣṇu] stands at the door with his followers,
awaiting the proper time, placing the lords of sages at the forefront.
All those of noble vows who dwell across the fourteen worlds,
having heard [of it], have assembled today for the great festival of entrance.
Skanda said:
Having heard Nandin's words, the God, accompanied by the Goddess,
mounted his celestial chariot and departed from heaven.
Thus ends the ninety-seventh chapter, named “Description of the Sacred Field and Fords,” in the second half of the Kāśīkhaṇḍa, in the fourth [section] of the glorious Skandapurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

4.98.m: Listen, O fortunate Sūta, to the great festival of Śambhu
as it was related by Skanda to the jar-born [Agastya] when he questioned him.
Skanda said:
Listen, O wise one, to the story of Śambhu's entrance,
which brings joy to the three worlds and cuts down great sins.
Śambhu came from Mandara in Caitra on the Damanaka festival day;
having reached the Forest of Bliss, he wandered here and there.
Then, when the palace named Mokṣalakṣmīvilāsa reached completion,
the God entered the inner sanctum from the pedestal of the immaculate [seat].
On the first day of the bright fortnight of Kārttika, combined with Wednesday and the constellation Viśākhā,
when the Moon was in the seventh house and the other planets were in exaltation,
while musical instruments were played and the cardinal directions grew clear,
while all other sounds were drowned out by the chanting of the Vedas by the brahmins,
and the region between the earth and the atmospheric world echoed [with the noise],
everything was full of joy on the festive entrance of Śambhu.
Flocks of gandharvas sang, and troupes of apsarases danced;
the cāraṇas offered praises, and the hosts of gods rejoiced.
Fragrant breezes blew, and clouds rained flowers;
all wore auspicious dress, and all uttered words of blessing.
Everything stationary and moving became plump with bliss.
Among all the gods, asuras, gandharvas, and serpents,
among vidyādharas, sādhyas, kinnaras, and men,
and among all born as women and men, the four [aims of life] alone shone forth
completely unimpeded at every step.
The sky that was then tinged by masses of incense smoke, O sage,
does not abandon that dark blueness even today, at any time.
All the lamps that were lit at that time for the waving of lights —
their flames still shine in the sky today under the guise of stars.
On every mansion, variegated banners of various shapes,
brightened by the luster of beautiful flags, shone on every temple of Śiva.
In some places, skilled singers sang; in others, dancers danced;
and here and there, the four kinds of musical instruments were sounded.
On every road, the grounds were made slippery by sprays of sandalwood paste.

4.98.m: Displaying radiant colors of green, white, madder-red, blue, and yellow,

Paved floors of jewels gleamed on the tops of the gateways;

Even inanimate things then appeared as if they were endowed with life.
Whatever auspicious things are spoken of here, O jar-born [Agastya],
that day was indeed the very day of birth for all of them.
Arriving there, the God of gods then entered the Muktimaṇḍapa.

In the future Dvāpara age, O Hari, of this Kaivalyamaṇḍapa,
there will be this renown in the world: 'This is the Kukkuṭamaṇḍapa.'"

Then, having reached youth, when his father passed away,
he was driven to an improper place by the sharp arrows of the Love-god.

4.98.m: Urged by her and completely infatuated, he also drank what is undrinkable,

Seeing wealthy Vaiṣṇavas, he wore the guise of a Vaiṣṇava for a moment,
and the fool censured Śaivas, as if it were a means of saving from hell.

4.100.m: Sūta said:
Having heard this unexcelled Kāśīkhaṇḍa belonging to the Skanda [Purāṇa]—
I am exceedingly satisfied, and it has been retained in my heart.
The chapter containing the table of contents and the supreme māhātmya,
O son of Parāśara, relate this properly from the beginning as it occurred.
Vyāsa said:
Pay heed, O righteous Sūta; listen, O Jātūkarṇya;
and let the young ones, Śuka, Vaiśampāyana, and the rest, also listen.
The chapter containing the table of contents and the māhātmya arising from the section,
I shall proclaim for the destruction of sin, increasing great merit.
The conversation between the Vindhya and Nārada is recounted in the first [chapter];
and the glory of Satyaloka is proclaimed as the second.
Then the arrival of the gods at the hermitage of Agastya;
the conduct of the devoted wife, and the departure of the pitcher-born [sage];
then the praise of sacred fords, and then the seven cities are recalled;
the nature of Saṃyaminī, and beyond that, the world of the sun;
then the attainment of the worlds of Indra and Agni by Śivaśarman;
after that, the origin of Agni, the origin of Kravyād and Varuṇa;
the origin of the two lords of the cities Gandhavatī and Alakā;
the attainment of the world of the moon by the twice-born Śivaśarman;
after that, the story of the world of stars, and then the origin of Śukra;
then the description of the worlds of Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn;

the consecration with four arms, and the final liberation of Śivaśarman;
the dialogue between Skanda and Agastya, and the origin of Maṇikarṇikā;
then the māhātmya of the Gaṅgā, and then the praise for Daśaharā;
the power of the Gaṅgā, and the thousand names of the Gaṅgā;
then the praise of Vārāṇasī, and then the manifestation of Bhairava;
the emergence of Daṇḍapāṇi, and then the origin of Jñānavāpī;
the narrative of Kalāvatī, and after that, proper conduct;
the section on the celibate student, and then the characteristics of women;

the sacred ford Daśāśvamedhika, and the arrival of the gaṇas from Mandara;

then the origin of Pañcanada, and the emergence of Bindumādhava;
then the detailed description of the māhātmya of the Vaiṣṇava sacred fords;
the journey of the trident-bearer with the bull-banner from Mandara to Kāśī;
the conversation of the great Lord with Jaigīṣavya at Jyeṣṭhasthāna;
then the recounting of the secret of the sacred field, which destroys sin;
then the origin of Kandukeśa and Vyāghreśa;
then the story of Śaileśvara, and the sight of Ratneśa;
the emergence of Kṛttivāsas, and then the arrival at the shrines;
the residence of the deities, and the prowess of the demon Durgāsura;
the victory of Durgā, and then the description of Oṃkāra;
again the māhātmya of Oṃkāra, and the origin of Trilocana;

then the glory of Dharmeśa, and then the auspicious story of the bird;
then the narrative of Viśvabhuja, and then the story of Durdama;
then the narrative of Vīreśvara, and further the glory of Vīreśa;

the glory of Viśvakarma-īśa, and the undertaking of Dakṣa's sacrifice;
the shedding of the body by Satī, and then the emergence of Dakṣeśvara.
Then indeed the proclamation of the greatness of Pārvatīśa,
and next the greatness of Gaṅgeśa, [and] the origin of Narmadeśa,
the origin of Satīśvara, the description of Amṛteśa and others,
the paralysis of Vyāsa's arm, and the release from Vyāsa's curse,
the collection of sacred fields and sacred fords, the discourse on the Muktimaṇḍapa,
and the manifestation of Viśveśa, followed by the circuit of pilgrimage.
This century of narratives has been proclaimed in order,
by merely hearing which the fruit of hearing all the sections [is gained].
Even in this chapter of the index of contents, the circuit of pilgrimage is [set forth].
Sūta said:
Tell the circuit of pilgrimage for the sake of the welfare of people,
duly for those desiring attainment, O best of the sons of Satyavatī.
Vyāsa said:
Listen, O very wise Lomaharṣaṇa, I will tell you
how the pilgrimage should first be performed with joy by pilgrims.
Having first bathed together with one's clothes in the waters of Cakrapuṣkariṇī,
and having gratified the gods, ancestors, brahmins, and beggars,
having bowed to the sun, Draupadī, Viṣṇu, Daṇḍapāṇi, and Maheśvara,
one should then go to see Ḍhuṇḍhivināyaka.
Having sipped water at Jñānavāpī, one should then worship Nandikeśa;
having then worshipped Tārakeśa, [one should worship] Mahākāleśvara next,
and then Daṇḍapāṇi again. This is the pilgrimage to the five sacred fords.
It should be performed daily by those who desire great fruit.
